title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing, fairness, starvation prevention, and improved timeouts
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: Under mixed-latency workloads we observed request starvation and long tail latency due to continuous-batcher scheduler behavior: long-running batched requests could monopolize slots and short interactive requests would wait past useful timeouts. This PR tunes the continuous-batcher scheduler to improve queueing fairness, prevent starvation, and make timeouts more predictable across tenant and priority classes.

Summary of changes: Implements a priority-aging mechanism (dynamic priority boosting) for queued requests so that older requests gain scheduling weight over time; switches to a token-aware fairness policy that accounts for expected token cost rather than just request count; adds per-queue soft timeouts with conservative early-fallback windows to avoid long head-of-line blocking; pins hot KV-cached prefixes for short interactive requests to reduce eviction thrash; emits new metrics to reason about queue depth, age-percentile, and starvation events; and adds a deterministic simulation harness and stress e2e tests exercised in bench-lab.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement priority aging and token-aware fairness
- [x] Add configurable soft timeouts and early-fallback heuristics
- [x] Emit observability (metrics/traces) and dashboard docs
- [x] Add unit + integration tests + bench harness scenarios
- [x] Run perf benchmarks and adjust defaults based on lab results

Design notes: The scheduler now computes an effective_score = base_priority + age*age_weight - estimated_token_cost*cost_weight. Age_weight and cost_weight are tunable cluster-wide parameters (defaults chosen after bench-lab runs). The soft timeout is expressed as a fraction of model SLO (e.g., 0.6 * expected_tail_latency) and triggers an early fallback path that either: a) route to a lower-cost model variant, or b) trigger a cached KV-prefix answer for idempotent prompts. Early-fallback decisions are conservative by default to preserve accuracy for mainline requests.

KV cache pinning: For short-interactive requests (<=32 tokens history, high qps), the scheduler may pin the KV cache for the life of a short window to avoid repeated cache warmups. Pinning has safeguards: eviction thresholds, per-model pin budget, and a short TTL to avoid memory leak.

Observability: Adds metrics: continuous_batcher.queue_depth_by_priority, continuous_batcher.age_p50_p95, continuous_batcher.starvation_events{tenant}, continuous_batcher.effective_score_hist, continuous_batcher.soft_timeout_triggered. Traces include tags for effective_score and reason_for_fallback. Documentation added at docs/perf/continuous-batcher.md describing how to interpret metrics and recommended tuning values.

Testing: New unit tests for score computation and edge cases (very large token costs, negative priorities), a deterministic event-driven simulator (bench/continuous_batcher_sim.py) to reproduce starvation scenarios, and an e2e stress test that runs in bench-lab with mixed short/long workloads. Bench results (attached in bench-lab run) show 25-40% reduction in 99th percentile latency for short requests under mixed load and no measurable regression in mean latency for long-batch workloads.

Rollout plan: Feature guarded behind runtime flag continuous_batcher.scheduler.v2 with defaults flipped for dedicated clusters first. We will enable on canaries for 48h with the soft-timeout conservative defaults before broader rollout.

Related: ENG-3421 (continuous-batcher fairness improvements), ENG-3498 (kv cache stability), SUP-789 (support ticket with customer-reported starvation), previous PRs pr-28321 and pr-31024 for historical tuning context.

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps the scoring function linear for observability simplicity; follow-up work will explore ML-based admission scoring after more telemetry is collected.

review_comments: Jordan Kim: Can you justify the default age_weight choice? It looks high and might favor very old low-cost requests over new medium-cost ones.

Asha Patel (author): Age_weight was tuned in bench-lab across three workload mixes. Default chosen to reduce starvation in our most common mixed workload while keeping long-batch throughput within 5% of baseline. I added bench results and a short sensitivity table in docs/perf/continuous-batcher.md.
Priya Nair: KV pinning looks useful but I'm worried about memory pressure in dense multi-tenant hosts. Do we have guardrails?

Asha Patel (author): Added per-model pin budget and a cluster-level pin_memory_limit. Pin entries also have a TTL and are evicted under pressure; noted these safeguards in code comments and docs. Also added unit test for eviction under pressure.
Ethan Wang: The soft timeout window may cause premature fallbacks for models with high variance. Can we make the fraction model-specific?
Asha Patel (author): Implemented model-specific override in config and added a feature flag to enable per-model SLO fractions. Kept cluster default conservative.

release_notes: Scheduler: improved fairness and starvation prevention in continuous-batcher. Introduces priority-aging and token-aware fairness, soft timeouts, KV cache pinning. Backwards compatible; feature gated behind continuous_batcher.scheduler.v2. Recommended: enable on canaries and monitor continuous_batcher.starvation_events and age percentiles.
bench_results_summary: 25-40% reduction in p99 latency for short requests under mixed workloads; mean latency for long-batch workload within 5% of baseline. Detailed artifacts attached to bench-lab run.
